item.title: Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will come on Tuesday. CAS’s ruling comes after a hearing of the case, over a chaotic AFCON final in January, which took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The parties have been notified that the CAS decision will be rendered Tuesday 24 November 2026 in the course of the afternoon (GMT),” CAS said in a short statement on Monday. At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. In response, the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) denounced the ruling as the “most blatant administrative robbery in the history of our sport”. The Senegal team even paraded the trophy to their supporters in Paris at the end of March. The post Senegal to know fate of AFCON title appeal Tuesday – CAS appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fire Destroys Over 100 Shops At Kano Fish Market, Traders Count Losses
item.description: A fire outbreak at Kano Fish Market along Zaria Road has destroyed more than 100 shops, leaving traders counting losses estimated to run into billions of naira. The fire reportedly broke out at about 9:00 p.m. on Sunday, near Kano Line Motor Park, spreading across sections of the market and destroying shops, containers and goods. Reports indicate that approximately 150 shops and 200 containers were affected by the inferno, with some traders reportedly losing goods valued at millions of naira. Traders trying to salvage what is left after the fire One of the affected traders, Usman Sani, recounted how the fire spread through the market, destroying shops and goods before traders could salvage their belongings. “We received the news of the fire and rushed to the market, but by the time we got here, the flames had already spread. Many shops were affected, and traders lost goods worth millions of naira. The situation is heartbreaking,” he said. The huge fire on Sunday, November 22, 2026, as it razes the fish shop in Kano State. Another trader, Musa Inuwa, described the incident as a major setback for those who depend on the market for their livelihood. “Many of us depend entirely on this business to feed our families. We have lost our goods and capital, and we do not know where to start from. We are appealing to the government to come to our assistance,” he said. The affected traders are appealing to the Kano State Government and relevant authorities for urgent intervention to support those who lost their businesses. The Kano State Fire Service reportedly received a distress call at about 9:58 p.m. and deployed personnel to the scene, arriving four minutes later. Meanwhile, the cause of the fire remains unknown, as investigations continue. The post Fire Destroys Over 100 Shops At Kano Fish Market, Traders Count Losses appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: UK Digging New Reservoirs To Fight Persistent Droughts
item.description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the UK is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades. Bulldozers have been digging up the ground for the vast £800-million ($1 billion) Havant Thicket project near the southern coastal port of Portsmouth. Like much of Europe, Britain endured record-breaking heat this summer and, despite the return of rains as the country moves into winter, parts are still grappling with drought conditions. “We’ve got increasing problems with our water security in the UK,” climate scientist Hannah Cloke from Reading University told AFP. “We need to really think about how we’re storing that water because this problem is only going to get worse.” Scientists have warned extreme weather events are likely to become more frequent and more intense as the global climate changes. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP By mid-November, almost all of England remained in drought, with some areas classified as suffering severe drought, according to the Environment Agency. Potentially exacerbating matters, existing reservoirs were only 60 percent full, 19 percentage points below the seasonal average. For policymakers, the situation poses a longer-term challenge as the thirst for water increases with a rising population and the growth of heavy water-using industries such as data centres. Under England’s National Framework for Water Resources published in 2025, the country could face a daily water supply shortfall of five billion litres (1.3 billion gallons) by 2055, with resources under pressure. At the sprawling Havant Thicket site, Portsmouth Water chief executive Bob Taylor said the industry was waking up to the scale of the challenge after successive droughts and hot summers. Workers carry out construction work at the site of the new Havant Thicket Reservoir in Hampshire, southern England, on November 5, 2026. Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP The issue, he stressed, was not necessarily how much rain falls over the course of a year, but when it falls. Winters are becoming wetter, while summers are increasingly dry. “Without reservoirs you can’t store that intense rainfall and put it somewhere where it can be used at another time,” Taylor said. The new reservoir will eventually hold up to 8.7 billion litres of water, helping secure supplies for hundreds of thousands of people. Fed in part by winter surpluses from a major spring already tapped by Portsmouth Water, it has become one of the flagship projects in a broader shift in Britain’s water strategy. The government has approved the construction of nine major reservoirs by 2050, and last year relaxed planning rules to speed up projects after decades of under-investment in water infrastructure. Together, the future reservoirs could deliver an additional 670 million litres of water per day. ‘

item.title: Alleged Sexual Assault: Daura Emirate Probes Viral Video As Tourist Accuses Emir of Inappropriate Conduct
item.description: Tension has gripped Daura in Katsina State following the emergence of a viral video in which a foreign female tourist accused the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk, of inappropriate sexual conduct during a visit to his palace. The allegations, which have generated widespread reactions on social media, are currently under review by the Daura Emirate Council, which says it is investigating the authenticity of the video and the claims made by the tourist. The woman, identified as Mirka and known on Instagram by the handle @beduinqa, posted the video after completing a 30-day tour of different parts of Nigeria. In a statement accompanying the footage, she alleged that the incident occurred on Saturday, November 14, 2026, when she visited the Emir’s palace in Daura. According to her account, she was ushered into a large room where she met privately with the Emir. She alleged that during their conversation, the Emir held her hand and began playing with it despite her objections. Mirka claimed she repeatedly asked him to stop, writing: “I told him, ‘Your Highness, no, no, no. You should not be touching me like that.’ But he just laughed.” She further alleged that as the meeting ended, the Emir hugged her, kissed her on the cheeks and touched her breast without her consent. The tourist said the encounter left her shocked, disgusted and emotionally distressed, adding that it was the only alleged incident of sexual harassment she experienced throughout her month-long tour of Nigeria. She also claimed she was able to capture the encounter using a pair of Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses equipped with a built-in camera, and alleged that she may not have been the first woman to experience such conduct but might have been the first to record it. Reacting to the development, the spokesman of the Daura Emirate Council, Ibrahim Usman Murtala, confirmed in a telephone interview with our correspondent on Monday that the Emirate was aware of the viral video. Emir of Daura, Alhaji Dr. Faruk Umar Faruk He said the Emirate had commenced a review of the footage to determine its authenticity and ascertain whether it had been altered or manipulated using any form of technology. According to him, the Emirate will issue an official statement after concluding its internal review of the matter. As of the time of filing this report, neither the Emir of Daura nor the Daura Emirate Council had issued a substantive response to the specific allegations made by the tourist. Meanwhile, residents of Daura described the development as disturbing, saying allegations of such magnitude should be thoroughly investigated to establish the facts while safeguarding the integrity of Nigeria’s traditional institutions and ensuring justice for all parties involved. item.title: Ukraine Claims Strikes On Two Russian Boats Off Libya
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv. The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the frontlines. But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”. “It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” Zelensky wrote on X. This handout satellite photo taken and released by the Satellite image ©2026 Vantor shows the view of a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi port before a strike, on November 21, 2026. Photo by HANDOUT / SATELLITE IMAGE ©2026 VANTOR / AFP The Ukrainian leader claimed the Merkury was “one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war”. “Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he added. A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the strike on the Merkury, Zelensky said. Sunday’s strikes came after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, close to the waters of Finland, whose border guard said the strike was Ukrainian. The UN mission in Libya expressed “serious concern” over the attacks, calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”. “Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the UNSMIL wrote on X. item.title: India To Give $1.6b Aid Package To Flood-Hit Nepal
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighbouring Nepal on Monday in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods. “We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,” Modi said, standing alongside his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi. “To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees ($1.6 billion),” he said. India did not immediately give specific details of what the development package included. Shah was given a military honour guard parade at the presidential palace in New Delhi, on his first trip to a neighbouring country since taking office in March. Rescuers use an excavator to transport a flood survivor following flash floods and a landslide at Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026. Photo by PRAKASH MATHEMA / AFP The rapper-turned-politician came to power following a wave of youth-led anti-corruption protests in September 2025. Shah, 36, wearing his trademark sunglasses and dressed in black, was given a bear hug by Modi, 76, dressed all in white. Unlike his predecessors, Shah had initially refrained from foreign visits since becoming prime minister. His first overseas trip was to New York in September, where he addressed the United Nations General Assembly as Nepal reeled from a deadly tsunami-like flood, triggered by a high-altitude glacial mountain collapse, that killed more than 1,400 people and left 5,000 missing. ‘Deal with future disasters’ A man looks at the remains in the aftermath of flash floods at Trishuli in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 7, 2026. Photo by PEDRO PARDO / AFP Nepal, a largely rural country that contributes little to global greenhouse gas emissions, estimates reconstruction will cost $4.78 billion. Shah said it showed the “imperative to address the challenges of climate change through collective action”. In October, the United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund agreed the modest sum of $20 million in aid to Nepal — the maximum amount countries can request in a single application — and the first time it has set aside money for any country. Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan nation of 30 million people, has long had to balance its relations with its two giant neighbours, India and China. “Our commitment will be to help affected families rebuild their lives, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” Modi said. An aerial view shows a torrent of muddy water surging past houses and through the Trishuli river in the aftermath of flash floods, at Betrawati in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 29, 2026. item.title: Eisenkot, Netanyahu parties to meet again for Israel coalition talks
item.description: The parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot, who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, are due to resume coalition talks on Monday after negotiations a day earlier delivered no agreement. The third round of talks comes as Eisenkot’s wide-ranging camp faces divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu’s Likud. Former military chief Eisenkot has until December 6 — a deadline which can be extended by 14 days — to form a government to replace Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc. Delegations from Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party and Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud are due to meet on Monday evening for a third round of negotiations, a spokesperson for Likud told AFP. Representatives from each party met for nearly four hours on Sunday and laid out their positions “on a range of substantive issues,” with no sign of a breakthrough. – Political ‘boycotts’ – On Saturday, Yashar presented the talks as “a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government”, saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options. Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, including an end to “all personal attacks” and political “boycotts” targeting Netanyahu and his government. Eisenkot’s 48-member bloc needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority and remains divided over how to build a coalition. Short of 61 lawmakers, Eisenkot’s bloc could form a minority government. The head of the left-leaning Democrats party, Yair Golan, on Monday called for an end to the “sham talks with Likud”. Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel. Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political leverage against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023. But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot’s refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign. Last week, Eisenkot said that he would be prepared to put forward a minority national emergency government for a parliamentary vote should efforts to create a broad-based government fail. item.title: Bad COP, Worse COP: What’s Next After Climate Talks Fail?
item.description: The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries. The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies. It was an ignominious end for an unusual dual-presidency shared by Australia and Turkey, and negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, said it was “very disappointing”. For many observers, the outcome was the inevitable result of a process that has regularly been hamstrung by its insistence on consensus. “Decision-making that requires every country to agree on every comma is not fit for a climate emergency,” said Nikki Reisch, director of the Center of International Environmental Law’s climate and energy programme. Bowen identified the same issue. “The fundamental root of the problem is that when COP was created, for reasons I understand, it was made consensus only,” he said. “That’s a very tough ask.” ‘Significant reform’ COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. Sunday’s collapse has renewed calls for a reform to that consensus-based process, in which any one country, or a small minority, can nix progress. “It has been clear for years that the COP process is in need of significant reform,” wrote former US vice president Al Gore on X. He urged a “reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world.” But as Bowen noted, “you also need consensus to change consensus” — in other words, all countries would have to agree those reforms. He described that as a “particular challenge,” although others might characterise it as simply impossible. The COP31 talks deadlocked over multiple issues, notably whether the so-called cover decision would mention phasing out planet-warming fossil fuels. Several countries refused a deal without that mention, while others including Saudi Arabia were vehemently opposed to its inclusion. There were other serious faultlines, including the timing of scientific work from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and language on carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised by some as costly and ineffective. item.title: Nigeria not ready to host World Cup, says FIFA president
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently ready to host the FIFA World Cup, citing the need for investment in stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation infrastructure. Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News, aired on Monday, while responding to a question on what it would take for a country like Nigeria to host the global football tournament. “The key for hosting a World Cup is the infrastructure: the stadiums, hotels, airports, and transportation. This is where the investment is really necessary. “A country like Nigeria has the resources, the passion, and the will as well,” he said. Asked directly whether Nigeria was ready to host the World Cup, Infantino replied, “Today, no, but tomorrow, why not?” Nigeria last hosted a FIFA tournament in 2009, when it staged the FIFA U-17 World Cup, with Switzerland defeating Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets 1-0 in the final in Abuja. On his 10-year tenure as FIFA president, Infantino said the organisation’s growth and the expansion of its competitions reflected the work done under his leadership. “I think the facts really speak quite loudly here. Speak for themselves. The organisation of the World Cups, both for men and women, increasing the number of teams, increasing the competitive balance of these competitions, and the revenue news. “Of course, we moved from a bit more than 5 billion before I arrived to 16 billion in this last cycle,” he said. He added that football and FIFA had continued to grow, saying such progress required hard work and strict compliance with established standards. “Football is growing. FIFA is growing. This is not possible if you don’t work hard, but also if you don’t work in compliance with the highest possible standard,” he said. Infantino was in Nigeria over the weekend, where on Friday, he inspected the remodelled Warri City Stadium alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström. During the visit, h e praised Nigeria’s football heritage and the country’s contribution to the global game , noting that some of the world’s finest players came from Nigeria, particularly Delta State. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region. “Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said. At the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja, on Saturday, Infantino also commended President Bola Tinubu for investments in sports facilities, saying they demonstrated the country’s commitment to its young population. “He is doing, together with all of you, fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” he said. item.title: Nothing will stop 750km Coastal Highway – Umahi
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, declaring that nothing will stop the project. Umahi spoke during an inspection of bridges on Sections 1 and 2 of the highway. The disclosure was made in a statement by Francis Nwaze, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister, in Abuja on Monday. He quoted the minister as saying, “Nothing will happen to the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which passes through the nine coastal states. The President has directed that the project must be completed as envisaged.” Umahi described the highway as a profitable national investment capable of generating revenue, attracting private investors and unlocking tourism and industrial opportunities. “We are using concrete, and so we are entitled to carbon credits claim. We are also using solar instead of conventional electricity; we are entitled to carbon credits,” he said. He added that the superhighway would accommodate tourism facilities, factories, CCTV surveillance and other commercial infrastructure, with private investors already showing interest in recovering costs through investment arrangements. The minister disclosed that President Tinubu is expected to commission Section 1 this month or early December. He also clarified that the reconstruction of the East-West Road is an additional commitment by the President and does not replace or affect the Coastal Highway. He described the ongoing 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Road as another major infrastructure undertaking of the administration, stressing that Tinubu is pursuing multiple major projects simultaneously. Umahi commended the President for the scale of infrastructure development and economic reforms, citing declining inflation, improved foreign exchange access for businesses and the absence of ASUU strikes. He urged Nigerians, particularly South-East residents in Lagos, to support the President, noting that the administration has delivered significant infrastructure projects to the region. Meanwhile, Umahi has ordered a three-week nationwide emergency rehabilitation of major federal highways ahead of the festive season and the January 2027 elections. He directed Zonal Directors, Controllers, Resident Engineers and contractors to return to the field immediately to ensure critical roads are made motorable across all six geopolitical zones. “I feel so sad that a contractor will be on site doing permanent work, yet some sections of the roads remain impassable. This practice must stop,” he said. He warned that contractors must not allow motorists to suffer on failed sections while permanent construction continues, directing that damaged portions be excavated and rehabilitated using appropriate materials and asphalt where necessary. item.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992
item.description: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday. The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House. The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats. “House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X. Sunday’s result came after Foxx requested a recount. Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.” “Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices,” he added on X. The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. item.description: Nigerian Taiwo Awoniyi scored for Coventry City and later had to be substituted after collapsing in a Premier League victory over Crystal Palace at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) The striker scored his third goal for Coventry in a 3-2 win against bottom club Palace, but his afternoon came to a bizarre premature end. Awoniyi netted in the fifth minute with a close-range finish into the far corner from Jack Rudoni’s pass to put Coventry 1-0 up at the CBS Arena. But the 29-year-old, signed from Nottingham Forest in the close season, was forced to miss the last 45 minutes after going down clutching his leg in pain while the players were lining up to start the second half. Awoniyi had to be helped up off the ground by two Palace players and limped off, forcing bemused Coventry boss Frank Lampard to make an unexpected substitution. Lampard admitted afterwards that Awoniyi felt a slight problem with his ankle from the first half. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri struck twice in the opening stages to help Santander beat Real Sociedad 3-2 in La Liga. The 21-year-old, on loan from Rennes, climbed to 11 league goals and trails only Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe in the Spanish scoring charts. Zabiri smashed home in the sixth minute for the opener and two minutes later was alert to pinch the ball from Real Sociedad’s goalkeeper and roll it into the empty net for his second. GERMANY JUMA BAH (Augsburg) Sierra Leone and Augsburg centre-back Bah netted his first goal since arriving on a season-long loan from Manchester City in his side’s 3-1 home romp over Mainz in the Bundesliga. With Augsburg 1-0 up, Bah was on the spot to prod a loose ball across the line from a corner to give the hosts their second. FRANCE PATRICK ZABI (Paris FC) Ivorian Zabi opened the scoring just after half-time as second-placed Paris FC hammered lowly visitors Angers 4-0 to lie second in Ligue 1 after 11 rounds, three points behind European champions Paris Saint-Germain. A cross was nodded into the path of the 20-year-old, and he slammed the ball into the net. BOULAYE DIA (Lorient) Dia, a 2022 Africa Cup of Nations champion with Senegal, put Lorient ahead away to Rennes in a 1-1 draw between mid-table clubs. Tunisian Montassar Talbi equalised in the final minute of the first half. The post African players in Europe: Mixed fortunes for Nigerian Awoniyi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu won’t be included in my national unity govt — Makinde
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has ruled out including President Bola Tinubu in his proposed government of national unity if elected in 2027, accusing the president of failing to honour an agreement they reached ahead of the 2023 election. Makinde, however, said he would consider appointing capable members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) into his government, insisting that there were decent people in the ruling party who could contribute to governance. He stated this during an interview on The Rooftop Podcast, where he was asked whether he would bring former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Tinubu into his government if elected. “Perhaps not President Tinubu, but there are still decent people in APC as well. I’ll tap them and they are Nigerians,” Makinde said. Asked whether he did not consider Tinubu decent, the governor said his position was informed by his experience working with the president during the 2023 election, when an agreement on a government of national unity was allegedly reached but not fulfilled. “Well, not in that context. I mean, I worked for him in 2023. We agreed on a government of national unity. He did not fulfil it,” he said. Makinde explained that the agreement was part of the position taken by the PDP G5 governors, who broke ranks with the party’s leadership ahead of the 2023 presidential election, saying they wanted an inclusive government that would draw competent Nigerians from across the country, irrespective of political affiliation. “We came from the PDP as G5 and we said, ‘Look, this is not going to be a government of APC. It should be a government where you tap people from all across the country. Go to every corner of the country, pick and choose people that can help you know to sort some of this out,’” he said. The APM candidate said the idea of a government of national unity was not new, citing the administration of the late military Head of State, General Sani Abacha, as an example of efforts to bring prominent Nigerians into government to ease political tensions. He recalled that following the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, Abacha appointed prominent figures, including former Lagos State governor Lateef Jakande and businessman Alex Ibru, to his government. Makinde said the appointments were intended to calm tensions and pacify aggrieved Nigerians. “And it’s been done before. After the annulment of the June 12, 1993 elections, and General Abacha came into government, they went and tapped Alhaji Jakande, Alex Ibru, all of those were geared towards bringing down the temperature in the country and ensuring that where there are angry people, they are being pacified,” he said. item.title: Tourist accuses Daura Emir of sexual assault
item.description: The Emir of Daura, His Royal Highness Alhaji Faruq Umar-Faruk, has been embroiled in an alleged sexual assault of a foreign tourist who visited his palace in Daura, Katsina State, during her tour of Nigeria. The tourist, who identified herself on Instagram as @beduinqa, alleged in a viral video that the 92-year-old monarch fondled her hand and other body parts. The video has elicited reactions, with Amnesty International Nigeria and prominent voices in the North calling for a thorough probe into the act. When contacted, the Daura Emirate spokesperson (Sarkin Labarai), Ibrahim Murtala, confirmed that the Emirate has seen the video and they are currently analyzing its content, adding that the Emirate will address the matter after the conclusion of the ongoing processes. Defence ministry stirs controversy over APC rally posts Niger: 64 killed in reprisal over village head’s murder As of the time of filing this report, the state government had not issued any statement on the alleged sexual assault by the monarch. Attempts to reach the state Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Alhaji Bashir Tanimu, to comment on the matter failed as calls put through to his mobile phone were unanswered. He did not respond to a text message sent to him either. The Katsina State Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu, said the command was not aware of the video and did not receive any formal complaint from anyone on the matter. Describing the alleged experience, the tourist said she found it disgusting and had continued to think about what happened. She explained that although the incident occurred on November 14, she chose not to make it public until she had completed her tour and left the country. In a post shared on her Instagram page alongside the video, the tourist wrote: “Recently I finished 30 days journey exploring all around #Nigeria. I had amazing time, saw beautiful places, met great people. “Unfortunately I had also a bad experience when visiting #daura in Northern Nigeria. During visit to the #emirofdaura palace I was taken to an elegant room where we sat on a couch and started talking. It was strange for me that he grabbed my hand and started playing with it. “Then when we stood up, he hugged me, kissed my cheek (which was also surprising for me), and then he grabbed my boobs. That was a shock for me. I told him “emir no, no, no, no” “emir you cannot be touching”, but he was just laughing about it. “I wasn’t sexually assaulted at any moment when walking through streets of Nigeria, even in busy crowded places, but to my shock I was assaulted in a palace by a traditional leader who should be behaving in exemplary and dignified way.” The tourist also suggested that she might not have been the first woman to experience such conduct from the Emir. “I suspect I wasn’t first woman he assaulted but probably first one with a proof recorded. item.title: 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde
item.description: By Bayo Wahab Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has explained why Nigerians should choose his ticket with former Kano State governor, Ibrahim Shekarau’s associate Daura, over the Peter Obi-Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket in the 2027 presidential election. Makinde cited the historic alliance between the Southwest and North, his experience in governance, youthful energy and plans for national unity as key advantages of his candidacy. Speaking on The Rooftop Podcast, the governor said the relationship between the two regions had helped Nigeria maintain stability during difficult periods, arguing that his ticket was positioned to sustain that tradition. “Apart from the traditional Southwest-North alliance, because that alliance has always provided stability for Nigeria in time of crisis in the past,” Makinde said. He recalled Nigeria’s first military coup, arguing that the Southwest and North had historically played significant roles in efforts to preserve the country’s stability. “If you even go back to the first military coup in Nigeria, the people that were wasted were basically the north and southwest, because we’re always in the forefront of stability for the country, and that is what we have brought to the table,” he said. Makinde also pointed to his performance in Oyo State and what he described as the youthful energy of his ticket, saying his administration’s achievements and commitments could be measured against documented promises. He said his political agenda was designed to allow Nigerians hold him accountable for his promises, rather than rely solely on campaign rhetoric. The APM candidate also outlined his proposed transitional government of national unity, saying it would address Nigeria’s political and security challenges through a broader national consensus. Makinde said he was willing to lead such a transition but would not remain in office to benefit from its eventual outcome, arguing that doing so could compromise his decisions. “I can lead it, but I will not be a beneficiary of the outcome because if I’m looking at myself benefiting from that outcome, it may cloud my judgment and also block how I will take that decision,” he said. He said the proposed arrangement was necessary because insecurity and other problems affecting Nigeria were not confined to any particular region. “And a government of national unity, because, you know, you look at insecurity and things fueling it all around the country. It’s not limited to any area,” Makinde said. The post 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kwankwaso broke APC defection pact with Tinubu — Abba
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has accused his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of reneging on an agreement to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election. Yusuf, who made the allegation in an interview with BBC Hausa, said Kwankwaso personally asked him to approach President Bola Tinubu and assure him that they would join the APC if the President did not interfere in the legal battle over the Kano governorship election. The governor said the agreement was reached after the 2023 election, when his victory over the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna, was being challenged in court. According to Yusuf, Kwankwaso initiated the arrangement and asked him to swear by the Holy Qur’an that they would return to the APC if the judicial process was allowed to run its course without interference. “Kwankwaso himself sent me to Tinubu and asked me to tell him that we had made that promise. He even wanted me to swear by the Holy Qur’an that if God granted us victory, we would all come together,” Yusuf told the BBC. He said he honoured the agreement and subsequently assured Tinubu of their intention to defect. Yusuf added that Kwankwaso also held several meetings with the President and sent delegations to discuss the proposed political realignment. The governor, who formally defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) to the APC on January 26, 2026, insisted that he did not betray his former political benefactor but fulfilled an agreement that Kwankwaso later abandoned. He also dismissed suggestions that his defection was a political arrangement aimed at weakening the opposition or distracting the public, maintaining that Kwankwaso was aware of the discussions and arrangements leading to the move. Yusuf, however, said some remarks allegedly made by Kwankwaso shortly after he had assured Tinubu of their planned defection undermined the arrangement. He said the comments were communicated to the President and reportedly did not go down well with him. On his relationship with Kwankwaso since their political separation, Yusuf said they had occasionally communicated, adding that he sometimes sent messages to greet his former mentor. He declined to discuss publicly allegations that Kwankwaso had exerted undue influence over his administration or prevented him from exercising his responsibilities as governor, saying such matters were better left outside the media. Marital crisis The governor also spoke about the reported marital crisis between him and his wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, a niece of the former Kano governor. Yusuf said their marriage, which began about 20 years ago, produced children, but difficulties eventually emerged in their relationship. He alleged that his wife’s belongings were removed from his residence and that she was taken away without his knowledge. item.title: Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦80,000 military fare
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces. The committee also urged other airlines and corporate organisations in the country to emulate the gesture as part of efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel and veterans. The commendation was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Chairman of the committee, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, representing Katsina Central Senatorial District. According to the statement, the initiative was unveiled on November 16, 2026, during the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja. The committee said the discounted fare was available to eligible military personnel who had served in the Nigerian Armed Forces since 1960, across all domestic routes. It added that Air Peace would also bear the cost of tickets for regional and international flights, with beneficiaries required to pay only applicable taxes and charges. Describing the initiative as a patriotic gesture, the committee said it was a practical demonstration of appreciation for the sacrifices made by serving and retired military personnel in defending the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It noted that members of the Armed Forces had continued to make enormous sacrifices, often at great personal cost, and deserved tangible support that would improve their welfare and that of their families. “By reducing the burden of air travel, Air Peace has demonstrated that patriotism is not only spoken in times of ceremony, but shown in practical action that touches the lives of those who serve,” the statement said. The committee particularly praised Onyema for what it described as his consistent commitment to humanitarian causes, national development and support for the Nigerian military. It also endorsed the airline chairman’s call for the military leadership to establish a robust verification system to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries access the concession. According to the committee, such a mechanism would help make the initiative sustainable, transparent and free from abuse. It appealed to other airlines and corporate organisations to support the Armed Forces, describing the welfare of serving personnel and veterans as a collective national responsibility. “The private sector has a critical role to play in complementing the efforts of the Federal Government in improving the welfare and morale of our troops and veterans,” it said. The Senate committee assured Air Peace of its support and readiness to work with the airline, the Ministry of Defence and the Service Chiefs to ensure the smooth implementation of the initiative. It reiterated its appreciation to the airline’s management for the gesture, describing it as a meaningful tribute to Nigeria’s military personnel. The post Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦

item.title: FG partners world’s largest pivot irrigation maker
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme. The agreement also provides for the establishment of an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria in partnership with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), as part of efforts to boost local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported irrigation technology. The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) signed the agreement with Valmont at the weekend. In a statement issued by NASENI on Sunday, the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, said the agreement formally brought Valmont, through its Valley Irrigation brand, on board as a major partner in developing irrigation infrastructure across the country. Muhammed, who signed the agreement alongside Valmont’s Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Africa, Mr Kalle Autto, described the partnership as a significant step towards expanding mechanised irrigation in Nigeria. He said: “This MoU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.” He explained that beyond developing irrigation infrastructure, Valmont had agreed to work with NASENI to establish a local production facility for irrigation equipment. “Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” he added. The agreement also provides for a pilot irrigation programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State. The project will be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF). While PICTT will lead the overall implementation of the programme, NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology. The partnership is also expected to create opportunities for collaboration with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute on sustainable irrigation systems and water resource management. Muhammed said key stakeholders had already expressed interest in expanding irrigation infrastructure through the partnership, describing the development as a vote of confidence in the programme. Officials said the agreement would help improve agricultural productivity, strengthen national food security and promote the sustainable management of water resources in line with the Federal Government’s agricultural transformation agenda. item.title: Troops rescue 18 abducted children, hunt for four others in Kaduna
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers. The children, members of the Boys’ and Girls’ Brigade, were reportedly abducted early Sunday, November 22, 2026, while participating in a morning group road walk at Mother-Cat Community in the Kachia/Kajuru general area of the state. Confirming the rescue in a statement on Sunday night, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said troops of the 1 Division Nigerian Army, operating under Sector 1 of Operation Fansan Yamma, launched a rescue operation shortly after receiving a distress call. Anele said troops of Sub-Sector 5 immediately mobilised and pursued the abductors through surrounding bushes, advancing towards Rehina Riverside, where some of the children were found abandoned by the fleeing criminals. She said the troops sustained the pursuit along the river line, rescuing additional victims and bringing the number of recovered children to 18. According to the Army, sustained military pressure forced the abductors to abandon the children as they fled deeper into the surrounding forest. The statement added that troops had extended their search operations along the Ankwa–Kabode–Pachi link road and towards the Awon and Akwondo general areas to locate the remaining four children and apprehend those responsible for the abduction. The Army assured the families of the victims and the general public of its commitment to rescuing all the abducted children. It also said troops would sustain offensive operations and intelligence-led patrols to protect vulnerable communities and prevent further attacks. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support the ongoing search-and-rescue operations and facilitate the arrest of the perpetrators. item.title: GAS: Domestic market gets 41.3% as Nigeria’s supply averages 4.95bcf/d in 10 months
item.description: •LPG retail price rises 12.5% to N1,800 per kg •Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM By Udeme Akpan Despite Nigeria’s 215.19 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of proven natural gas reserves, the domestic market received an average of 2.04 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d), representing 41.3 per cent of the country’s total supply of 4.95 bcf/d in the first 10 months of 2026. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest report obtained by Vanguard. The report showed that the Nigeria LNG Limited, NLNG, received the remaining 58.7 per cent, averaging 2.91 bcf/d. In October, total average daily gas supply rose by 2.7 per cent to 4.951 bcf/d, from 4.822 bcf/d in September. Domestic supply increased by 2.3 per cent to 2.113 bcf/d, while deliveries to NLNG grew by three per cent to 2.838 bcf/d. April recorded the highest average daily supply during the 10-month period at 5.141 bcf/d, comprising 2.01 bcf/d for domestic market and 3.13 bcf/d for NLNG. Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. Supply to the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids facility fell by two per cent. Gas exports also strengthened. Average daily LNG exports increased by seven per cent to 52,721 metric tonnes per day, from 49,198 metric tonnes per day in September, while pipeline exports through the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP) rose by 11 per cent to 0.149 bcf/d, from 0.134 bcf/d. LPG retail price rises 12.5% to ₦1,800 per kg Meanwhile, the average retail price of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, also known as cooking gas, rose by 12.5 per cent to ₦1,800 per kilogramme in November 2026, from ₦1,600 in October. Checks by Vanguard attributed the increase largely to limited supply. The average depot price of LPG stood at ₦1,274 in the Daily Depot Price Intelligence Report for Friday, November 20, 2026. The report covered Lagos, Warri, Calabar and Port Harcourt but did not provide a regional breakdown of LPG prices. item.title: President Tinubu does not need this falsehood
item.description: By Dele Sobowale Each time President Tinubu mentions $1 trillion economy by 2030, he reveals more than the politicians’ penchant for making promises they cannot keep. He brings into question his proclaimed economic qualification as an accounting graduate for a Chicago university. There is abundant evidence, provided by Tinubu himself, to call that assertion a deliberate lie. I have touched on some of them before; but, Tinubu, despite expert advice continues to campaign on a promise which can never be redeemed. Here again, the facts which Tinubu stubbornly ignores; because they don’t fit into the narratives of a desperate politician running for elections, will once more be presented. This time fresh evidence will be added from Tinubu’s campaign organization. POLITICS AND FALSEHOOD ARE INSEPRABLE “The great masses of the people ..will fall victims to a great lie than to a small one.” Adolf Hitler, 1899-1945, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS, VBQ p 130. Politicians, under the best of circumstances, would repeat the same falsehood in the hope that saying it long enough will make it true. And, when they fail, they never apologise to the people; they blame others. President Tinubu’s assertion that Nigeria’s economy can grow to $1 trillion by 2030 is the sort of thing Hitler was talking about. I have given Tinubu the benefit of doubt that he read accounting in an American university as an undergraduate. But, his insistence that the Nigerian economy, whose Gross Domestic Product, GDP, is estimated to reach $386.67 billion at the end of the year 2026 could reach $1 trillion in just four years, would have had first year students of any university wondering if that was a joke or something else not hilarious. The figures don’t add up. LIARS CAN FIGURE; FIGURES DON’T LIE “Every government is run by liars and nothing they say should be believed. I.F Stone, 1907-1989. US Journalist and Publisher. Stone was one of my favourite columnists during my ten years in the US. I read his articles as if preparing for an examination on the subject discussed. He always led with evidence. So, let us start with the Federal Governments own figures. President Tinubu has been going round the country telling Nigerians the Nigerian economy is set to grow by 4.5 per cent this year. That will be the best performance since 2014. It is admittedly very commendable but worse than Jonathan’s worst year. The FG is also promising 6 percent growth in 2027. Highly praise-worthy if achieved. For some reason, not too difficult to understand, Tinubu, a self-proclaimed accountant, as well as his mob of supporters, cannot seem to understand that you cannot grow $386.67 billion to $1 trillion at 6 per cent in four years. This is primary school arithmetic called compound interest calculations. It is repeated at freshman level in American universities.
